messages.subject: Emptying read-only variables
parts:
Hello!

First of all greetings to all of the developers and users of such an awesome tool! My name is Carlos and I am designing a dynamic browser for a database. I'm still learning how to use shiny so I apologize beforehand if I ask something too obvious. My main question is if there is a way to empty a read-only variable (generated via input) or to clear all of the variables in a session given a trigger (for example deleting a letter from a textInput box). I'll try to explain why I want to do that in the following lines.

The application has a text box where an user inputs its query. Next the application searches for matches to that query, if an exact match is identified a table with results is presented. If no exact matches are found all non-exact matches are presented using a dynamic selectInput generated by renderUI. After the user selects one desired match, the table with results is presented. The problem is that when the user tries to perform another search (without refreshing the browser) the variable containing the output of the dynamic selectInput still contains a value which is presented, regardless of the text in the textInput box. I find it impossible to empty that variable or store it in another place given that my variables are reactive and linked. That is the reason I am looking for a way to empty the read-only variable containing the selected selectInput (or all of the variables in a session given that the user starts erasing text from the textInput box).


Thank you in advance for the help!

Carlos

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: Emptying read-only variables
parts:
There is a function called updateSelectInput which can used similar to the below

 updateSelectInput(session = session, inputId = "myselection",
      choices = c("Choice A" = "a", "Choice B" = "b"),
      selected = "Choice B")
  })

I guess it's possible to empty your selectInput by setting choices = "", selected = ""

Hopefully this is what you were looking for.

parts:
Thank you for your quick reply. I tried generating a simple example which I will paste below. I wasn't able to use updateSelectInput, I'm not sure why, I thought it could be an issue with the outputOptions but it seems that wasn't the case either. Any idea of what could be the problem?

Thanks a lot!


The problem case is when you search for "a " (a and a blank space). It will display two options and once you select one it will stay stuck in the same option unless you refresh.

--- ui.R---
shinyUI(
  bootstrapPage(
    textInput("what", "Search:"),
    conditionalPanel(condition = 'length(find()) == 1', h4(textOutput('caption'))),
    conditionalPanel(condition = 'length(find()) != 1', htmlOutput("selectUI")),
    conditionalPanel(condition = '1 == 1', h4(textOutput('level')))
  )
)
---------

---server.R---
sample <- c("a", "a b", "a c", "ab")

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  find <- reactive({
    if(nchar(input$what) > 0){
      if(length(input$options) != 1){
        exact <- grep(paste("^", input$what, "$", sep = ""), sample, ignore.case = TRUE)
        if(length(exact) == 1){
          exact
        } else{
          exact <- grep(paste(input$what, sep = ""), sample, ignore.case = TRUE)
        }
      } else{
        input$options
      }
    } else{
      updateSelectInput(session, "options", choices = "", selected = "")
    }
  })
  output$level <- renderText({
   class(input$options)
  })
  output$caption <- renderText({
    if(length(find()) == 1){
      find()
    } else{
      'Select element:'
    }
  })
  output$selectUI <- renderUI({
    if(length(find()) > 1){
      current <- find()
      names(current) <- sample[current]
      selectInput("options", "Select your choice:", current, multiple = TRUE)
    }
  })
  #outputOptions(output, "selectUI", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)
})
------

I think your conditional panel don't work. I think you need to put into the condition some JavaScript instead of R code. Pro-shiner please correct me if I am wrong.

Now I think this is what you are looking for except the hiding select element part.

A few things I will explain which I think will help you understand this better

  • If you want to use updateSelectInput then you can skip having a renderUi in server.R, just place your selectInput into your ui.R and use updateSelectInput to update the choices
  • In your original code the reactive dependencies was causing the undesirable effect you saw. It was like this: find() reacts to changes to input$what but also to input$options. Now once one of the input$options is selected find() will recalculate! When it recalculates it outputs the selected options, which then causes selectUi to recalculate. Now because you have selected something this caused find() to return just 1 number instead of 2. So this caused lenght(find()) return 1 which means your selectInput is no longer rendered because you don't render it unless length(find()) > 1 (see your selectUi code)

I suggest this, make find() a function that returns all the matches and have another reactive find1() to return a selected option instead of using find(). So find() remains static unless input$what is changed. This solves the undesirable reactive dependencies you saw. Also The reactive log can help you diagnose such problems

From ?showReactLog:

To use the reactive log visualizer, start with a fresh R session and run the command options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE); then launch your application in the usual way (e.g. using runApp). At any time you can hit Ctrl+F3 (or for Mac users, Command+F3) in your web browser to launch the reactive log visualization.

I think the main problem is that the find() reactive was serving too many purposes. I found it much easier to break it up into different jobs.

I also changed the problem around so that selecting a choices from the selectInput put the corresponding value into the textInput. I think that is more clear to the user anyway.

Now I think this is what you are looking for except the hiding select element part.

A few things I will explain which I think will help you understand this better

  • If you want to use updateSelectInput then you can skip having a renderUi in server.R, just place your selectInput into your ui.R and use updateSelectInput to update the choices
  • In your original code the reactive dependencies was causing the undesirable effect you saw. It was like this: find() reacts to changes to input$what but also to input$options. Now once one of the input$options is selected find() will recalculate! When it recalculates it outputs the selected options, which then causes selectUi to recalculate. Now because you have selected something this caused find() to return just 1 number instead of 2. So this caused lenght(find()) return 1 which means your selectInput is no longer rendered because you don't render it unless length(find()) > 1 (see your selectUi code)

I suggest this, make find() a function that returns all the matches and have another reactive find1() to return a selected option instead of using find(). So find() remains static unless input$what is changed. This solves the undesirable reactive dependencies you saw. Also The reactive log can help you diagnose such problems

sample <- c("a", "a b", "a c", "ab")
